working_title: The Night Brazil's Air Force Chased the Unknown

beats.narrative_function: Specific hook with a documented timestamp and immediate contradiction
beats.narration_en: At 11:15 p.m. on May 19, 1986, an official Brazilian report logged lights that pilots and controllers could not identify.
beats.visual_anchor: Primary archive table with the 19 May, 23:15, São José dos Campos entry; timestamp emphasized without adding unsupported graphics
beats.continuity_note: Open in darkness, then cut from document texture into the Brazilian night sky; no generic UFO illustration

beats.narrative_function: Place the mystery inside Brazil, not in an anonymous location
beats.narration_en: This was not a campfire legend from nowhere. It entered the records of Brazil’s air-defense system.
beats.visual_anchor: Night exterior of a geographically coherent Brazilian air-defense or air-base environment; no invented facility signage
beats.continuity_note: Keep the same night palette and restrained camera movement from S01

beats.narration_en: The National Archives says dozens of luminous objects appeared on CINDACTA radar, triggering an air-defense alert.
beats.visual_anchor: Archive page or verified document detail showing the official record; radar imagery only if sourced or labeled dramatization
beats.continuity_note: Document detail should carry the same cool, low-key night treatment

beats.narration_en: A pilot from Santa Cruz reported seeing one object low to his left after being ordered onto a new heading.
beats.visual_anchor: Faceless 1986-era pilot silhouette, shoulder and instrument panel only, aircraft turning at night
beats.continuity_note: Controlled realistic cockpit light; no visible face, no modern avionics, no alien craft

beats.narration_en: Then his onboard radar caught a contact between ten and twelve nautical miles away, matching what he could see.
beats.visual_anchor: Close-up of the primary report wording and a verified archive page; any radar visualization must be labeled if reconstructed
beats.continuity_note: Match the direction and distance language to the report; avoid a cinematic target lock that the document does not describe

beats.narrative_function: Escalate through motion and loss of control
beats.narration_en: According to the report, the object climbed from flight level 170 to 330, then moved beyond a twenty-mile range.
beats.visual_anchor: Faceless cockpit and distant light separating into darkness; no depiction of impossible physics as confirmed fact
beats.continuity_note: The light remains small and ambiguous; camera never reveals a definitive craft

beats.narration_en: Fighters launched from Santa Cruz and Anápolis with orders to approach and identify the targets.
beats.visual_anchor: Real Brazilian air-base exteriors or licensed aircraft imagery geographically and temporally contextualized; no unverified archival footage
beats.continuity_note: Move from cockpit darkness to exterior runway light, preserving night mood

beats.narrative_function: Create a credible contradiction and deepen the testimony
beats.narration_en: The pilot even looked away for a moment, trying to avoid a night-vision illusion. When he looked back, the light was pulsing green, red and white.
beats.visual_anchor: Faceless pilot gaze shifting from windscreen to instrument panel, then back to a distant pulsing light; color kept subdued
beats.continuity_note: No close-up of a colorful UFO; the colors remain a reported observation, not an objective design

beats.narration_en: A separate official table logged the São José dos Campos event as visible to pilots and controllers, by eye, binoculars and radar.
beats.visual_anchor: Archive table row with the observation methods readable, presented as a document rather than a flashy infographic
beats.continuity_note: Use a measured push-in that mirrors S01, making the file itself a recurring visual motif

beats.narration_en: Another report noted an unusual instrument indication, then its return to normal. It recorded the anomaly, but not its cause.
beats.visual_anchor: Primary report passage, with HSI and DME references shown only if legible and rights-cleared; no invented diagnostic overlay
beats.continuity_note: Return from document to low cockpit light without changing era or geography

beats.narrative_function: Protect truth boundary while preserving cinematic immersion
beats.narration_en: So what did the cockpit actually look like? We can only reconstruct it. This image is dramatized, not recovered footage.
beats.visual_anchor: Faceless cockpit reconstruction with a discreet DRAMATIZED REENACTMENT label
beats.continuity_note: Use the label only while the reconstruction is visible; maintain documentary treatment

beats.narrative_function: Make Brazil the protagonist and emotional center
beats.narration_en: That distinction matters. Brazil is not a backdrop here. Its pilots, controllers and archives are the evidence.
beats.visual_anchor: Brazilian landscape or air-base context connected directly to the documented institutions, never generic tropical filler
beats.continuity_note: Sustain the same night-to-dawn tonal progression; no abrupt tourist imagery

beats.narrative_function: Offer a rational alternative without collapsing the mystery
beats.narration_en: Maybe every light had a conventional explanation. But the surviving records do not identify one explanation for the whole night.
beats.visual_anchor: Faceless analyst or pilot silhouette studying the file, with no alien imagery and no explanatory text presented as fact
beats.continuity_note: Slow the camera and lower the sound bed before the final question

beats.narration_en: What exactly did those pilots chase, and why did the official file preserve the encounter without a final answer?
beats.visual_anchor: Brazilian night sky over a coherent real location, returning toward the archival document rather than revealing a craft
beats.continuity_note: Visual return echoes S02 and closes the geographic loop

beats.narrative_function: Emotional payoff and respect for the witnesses
beats.narration_en: For a few hours, Brazil’s defense system did what it was built to do: detect, respond and report. The mystery remained.
beats.visual_anchor: Restrained Brazilian dawn or air-base exterior, grounded and documentary, with the file motif lingering
beats.continuity_note: Resolve toward stillness, not spectacle; preserve space for CTA

beats.narration_en: For more Brazilian cases told with evidence, tension and no invented certainty, subscribe to Because Of This Stories.
beats.emotion_trigger: belonging and promise of consistent quality
beats.visual_anchor: Approved brand outro and final logo treatment
beats.continuity_note: No new story information; CTA begins only after the emotional payoff

fact_register.F-01: The Arquivo Nacional describes the event as occurring on 19 May 1986 and identifies it as the Noite Oficial dos OVNIs.
fact_register.F-02: The Arquivo Nacional page states that dozens of luminous objects were detected by CINDACTA radar and that an air-defense alert was triggered.
fact_register.F-03: The same official summary states that FAB aircraft departed Santa Cruz and Anápolis to approach and identify the objects.
fact_register.F-04: The official page identifies the image as a report made by a pilot from Anápolis who pursued one object.
fact_register.F-05: The documents belong to the Fundo Objeto Voador Não Identificado, produced by the Brazilian Air Force command and held by the Arquivo Nacional.
fact_register.F-06: The Santa Cruz report describes an initial visual contact after a commanded heading change and places the object low at one to two o'clock.
fact_register.F-07: The Santa Cruz report records an onboard radar contact at approximately ten to twelve nautical miles and a change from flight level 170 to 330 before the object moved beyond the stated range.
fact_register.F-08: The Santa Cruz report describes pulsating green, red and white colors after the pilot deliberately avoided fixing his sight continuously to reduce the chance of night-vision illusion.
fact_register.F-09: The Santa Cruz report records HSI and DME indications that later normalized; it does not establish a cause.
fact_register.F-10: The official occurrence table lists 19 May, 23:15, São José dos Campos, light, naked eye/binocular/radar, pilots/controllers.
fact_register.F-11: The same table lists an Anápolis light/radar occurrence at 01:10 on 20 May.
fact_register.F-12: A contemporary press record preserved in SIAN reports the alert and departures from Anápolis and Santa Cruz; it is used for fact cross-checking, not as a planned media asset.
